attempts.raw: The geometric meaning of a vector dot product is the projection of one vector onto another. It is a scalar quantity that represents the magnitude of the projection and the cosine of the angle between the vectors. The dot product of two vectors A and B is given by A · B = |A| |B| cos(θ), where |A| and |B| are the magnitudes of A and B, respectively, and θ is the angle between the vectors. If A and B are orthogonal, then cos(θ) = 0, and the dot product is zero. If A and B are parallel, then cos(θ) = ±1, and the dot product is ±|A| |B|. The negative projection of A onto B is given by -A · B / |B|, and the positive projection of A onto B is given by A · B / |B|.
